Democratic Convention Reform: More Blacks, Women and Youth
stories.summary: NY Times computer survey of initial 1/3 of delegates chosen for '72 Dem Natl Conv reveals that proportion of women is running at 3 times level of '68, that proportion of blacks is nearly double and proportion of other minorities is higher but that conv's composition as whole will fall short of reform guidlines estab by party; survey covers 1,034 delegates selected in 21 states and Washington, DC

stories.headline: Oppose Majority Ruling on Ground It Is Move for Racial Balance
stories.summary: US Sup Ct agrees on to uphold Fed Dist Ct decision that Emporia, Va, cannot secede from Greensville County because it would impede desegregation efforts; decision breaks long‐standing unanimity of Ct on desegregation when Nixon's 4 Ct nominees dissent against what they call effort to require racial balance rather than desegregation; dissent is 1st from Sup Ct ruling on integration since historic ‘54 ruling outlawing segregation; in companion case, Nixon appointees join majority in barring Scotland Neck, NC, from seceding from Halifax County under similar circumstances; school officials in both cases assert that result of secession would be more segregation, because increase of blacks over whites would cause whites to flee pss; all Justices agree that this is not acceptable reason for avoiding desegregation efforts; dissenting Justices are Chief Justice Burger and Justices Blackmun, Powell and Rehnquist

stories.headline: New Orleans Is Now Off Limits;Pentagon Joins in Relief Effort
stories.summary: New Orleans, which appeared to have narrowly escaped worst of Hurricane Katrina, is virtually submerged and isolated as water breaks through two levees, causing incalculable destruction and rendering city uninhabitable for weeks to come; bridges, highways and power and communications lines are washed out and officials order everyone still remaining out of city; about 10,000 refugees are to be evacuated from Superdome, where water and food are running out and rising water threatens generators; Pentagon orders five Navy ships and eight maritime rescue teams to Gulf Coast and will fly in Swift boat rescue teams from California; authorities can only guess at death toll, at least 100 in Mississippi alone, as efforts concentrate on finding the living, plucking them off rooftops in rescue cages; streets that were dry after storm passed are inundated as breaches in levees north of downtown send muddy waters of Lake Pontchartrain pouring into city; photos; map; charts; FEMA drops sandbags to try to seal breach; both airports are underwater as is 80 percent of city that lies below sea level; Gov Kathleen Blanco and other officials describe 'heartbreaking' situation; armed looters clean out stores for second night, critically wounding police officer; current damage estimates are over $25 billion; energy prices rocket with news of damage to oil and gas rigs in Gulf of Mexico; hundreds of critically-ill patients are evacuated from Tulane and Charity Hospitals and Times-Picayune staff flees newspaper's office; city from the air is shocking sight of utter demolition; entire areas of outlying parishes and Mississippi coast disappear under water; casino barges along river are swept half mile inland (L)

stories.headline: Congress to Investigate Whether Palmeiro Committed Perjury at Hearing
stories.summary: The leaders of a Congressional panel wrote to Major League Baseball yesterday to ask for a broad set of records related to Rafael Palmeiro's steroids suspension. Palmeiro independently said he would ''fully cooperate'' with the request and answer any further questions by any member of the House Committee on Government Reform, the group that he testified before in March, when he pointed his finger and adamantly denied ever using steroids.

stories.headline: Nielsen, Long a Gauge of Popularity, Fights to Preserve Its Own
stories.summary: Nielsen Media Research is trying to remake its image following controversy over whether its new local ratings system severely undercounted minority viewers, ultimately hindering development of programs geared to those audiences; company has spent over $4 million since spring of to hire premier lobbyists to counter campaign by News Corp and coalition of black and Hispanic leaders and more than $200,000 on outreach efforts to minority organizations; has had some public relations success, picking up support of Rev Jesse Jackson and working out reconciliation with Spanish-language broadcaster Univision Communications; but it still faces battle in Washington, where increased oversight is being considered; chart of lobbying expenses by single clients, in which Nielsen ranks seventh; photos (M)
